question: Which substances are selectively reabsorbed in the nephron?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Glucose, amino acids, and water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **nephron** is the functional unit of the kidney responsible for filtering blood and forming urine. Selective reabsorption occurs in the nephron to ensure essential substances are retained in the body.
 
• **Glucose**: Almost all glucose is reabsorbed in the proximal convoluted tubule of the nephron through active transport. This ensures glucose, a vital energy source, is not lost in urine.
 
• **Amino acids**: Similar to glucose, amino acids are also actively reabsorbed in the proximal convoluted tubule. These are essential building blocks of proteins and must be preserved for bodily functions.
 
• **Water**: Water reabsorption occurs throughout the nephron but primarily in the proximal tubule, loop of Henle, distal tubule, and collecting duct. This process is regulated by hormones like ADH (antidiuretic hormone) to maintain fluid balance in the body.
 
• The process of selective reabsorption ensures that waste products like urea and excess ions are excreted while essential substances like glucose, amino acids, and water are conserved.
 
• The correct answer highlights the substances crucial for maintaining homeostasis in the body through selective reabsorption in the nephron.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Urea and Carbon Dioxide**:

 
 
• **Urea**: It is a waste product formed in the liver during protein metabolism. Urea is not reabsorbed selectively; it is excreted in the urine.
 
• **Carbon dioxide**: This is a gaseous waste product expelled through the lungs and not filtered or reabsorbed in the nephron.
 
 
 
• **Bile and Hydrochloric Acid**:
 
 
• **Bile**: Produced by the liver and stored in the gallbladder, bile aids in digestion. It is not filtered by the kidneys or reabsorbed in the nephron.
 
• **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)**: Found in the stomach, HCl aids in digestion and is unrelated to kidney function.
 
 
 
• **Platelets and Enzymes**:
 
 
• **Platelets**: These are cellular components of blood involved in clotting and are too large to be filtered by the nephron.
 
• **Enzymes**: These are proteins that catalyze biochemical reactions. They are not filtered or reabsorbed in the nephron under normal conditions.
 
 
 
• **Other Key Functions of the Nephron**:
 
 
• The nephron regulates **salt and ion balance** through reabsorption of sodium, potassium, and chloride ions.
 
• It helps maintain **acid-base balance** by reabsorbing bicarbonate and secreting hydrogen ions.
 
• The kidneys also play a role in producing hormones like **erythropoietin** (stimulates red blood cell production) and **renin** (regulates blood pressure).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT)**: Reabsorbs 65-70% of filtered water, all glucose, and most amino acids and ions.
 
• **Loop of Henle**: Responsible for concentrating urine by creating a gradient for water and salt reabsorption.
 
• **Distal Convoluted Tubule (DCT)**: Fine-tunes ion and pH balance through selective ion exchange.
 
• **Collecting Duct**: Final site for water reabsorption, regulated by ADH, determining urine concentration.
